_help: One entry per test page at /coaching/<slug>/. 'format' facts come from the official test owner; keep 'source' and 'lastVerified' up to date. 'scoreBands' only lists thresholds published by a government or university, with the source. 'batches' is information from Wayfarer itself: set confirmed to true once the team has checked it.

options.name: Online batch
options.text: Live classes on your phone or laptop, with practice tests marked by a trainer.

options.name: Classroom batch at a branch
options.text: Classes at your nearest Wayfarer branch, with timings around college and work hours.

tests.name: IELTS
tests.whoFor: Students applying to the UK, Australia, Canada, Ireland, New Zealand and many US universities. IELTS for UKVI is the version used for UK visa purposes.

sections.name: Speaking
sections.detail: 11 to 14 minutes, face to face, 3 parts

format.scoring: Band 0 to 9 for each part, in half bands. The overall band is the average of the four parts.

scoreBands.label: UK Student visa (CEFR B2), IELTS for UKVI

faq.q: Which IELTS should I book for a UK student visa?
faq.a: If your university asks for a Secure English Language Test, book IELTS for UKVI (Academic). Many universities assess English themselves for degree courses and accept regular IELTS Academic, so check with your counsellor first.

faq.q: How long is an IELTS score valid?
faq.a: Universities and visa offices usually accept scores up to 2 years old. Check the rule for your university.

tests.name: PTE
tests.whoFor: Students applying to Australia, New Zealand, the UK and universities that accept PTE. The whole test, including speaking, is taken on a computer.

sections.name: Listening
sections.detail: Final part of the same sitting

format.scoring: 10 to 90 overall, on Pearson's Global Scale of English.

scoreBands.label: UK Student visa (CEFR B2), PTE Academic UKVI

faq.a: Neither is easier for everyone. PTE is fully computer-based, including speaking. Some students prefer that; others prefer speaking to a person. A free demo class helps you decide.

tests.name: TOEFL
tests.whoFor: Students applying mainly to US universities, and to other universities that accept TOEFL.

format.scoring: From 21 January 2026, scores are reported on a 1 to 6 scale in half points, aligned to CEFR. Until January 2028 you also get a comparable score on the old 0 to 120 scale.

scoreBands.label: Australia Student visa, TOEFL iBT (0 to 120 scale)
scoreBands.value: 67 overall. Select 'Taking TOEFL for Australia' when you register.

faq.q: My university asks for TOEFL 90. What is that on the new scale?
faq.a: Your score report shows both scales until January 2028, so you can compare directly. ETS publishes a concordance table on its website.

tests.name: Duolingo English Test
tests.whoFor: Students applying to universities that accept DET, mostly in the US. It is taken online at home. Check that your university and visa route accept it before booking.

sections.name: Adaptive test
sections.detail: 45 minutes, mixed reading, writing, listening and speaking tasks

format.scoring: 10 to 160 overall, in 5-point steps, with subscores.

faq.q: Can I use Duolingo for an Australian student visa?
faq.a: No. Australia does not accept English tests taken fully online at home for visa purposes.

tests.name: GRE
tests.whoFor: Students applying for master's and PhD programmes, mostly in the US. Some universities have made it optional; check each course.

format.scoring: Verbal and Quant: 130 to 170 each. Analytical Writing: 0 to 6 in half points.

faq.q: Is GRE compulsory for a US master's?
faq.a: Not always. Many universities have made it optional for some programmes. A good score can still help with admission and scholarships.

tests.name: GMAT
tests.whoFor: Students applying for MBA and business master's programmes.

format.duration: 2 hours 15 minutes, plus an optional 10-minute break
format.scoring: Total score 205 to 805. Each section is scored 60 to 90 and counts equally.

faq.q: Can I choose the order of sections?
faq.a: Yes. You can take the three sections in any order, and review and change up to three answers per section.

tests.name: SAT
tests.whoFor: 12th class students applying for bachelor's degrees in the US.

format.scoring: 400 to 1600 total. Each section is scored 200 to 800.

faq.q: When should I take the SAT?
faq.a: Ideally in Class 11 or early Class 12, so you have time to retake it before US application deadlines (usually November to January).
